correctness.rationale: Exact tr((B*B)^2) identifies the diagonal and distance-two contributions for arbitrary complex shift weights; phase independence follows from unitary diagonal conjugation. The full path-Jacobi spectrum gives the sharp constant, unique nonnegative Perron eigenvector, and next-eigenvalue quantitative deficit. An admissible positive second-eigenvector perturbation proves sharpness of the gap. For Schatten-fourth infinite shifts, Hilbert–Schmidt trace continuity and the exact discrete-gradient identity give strict nonattainment and approximating finite sine shifts. Endpoints n=2 and t=0,1 checked. Exact-rational matrix traces across 135 cases and independent complex-phase SVD tests corroborate but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: A natural first non-Hilbert even Schatten moment (p=4) creates an adjacency interaction absent at p=2. The closed formula solves a motivated operator-ideal optimization for every size and skew parameter, classifies all extremizing squared-weight shapes, quantifies near-extremizers sharply and separates finite attainment from an unattained infinite limit. It is not a reparametrized single matrix, tiny numerical gain or table replication: the normalized optimal profile changes with dimension and a genuine spectral gap governs rigidity.
